title: OpenAI ships a free CSAM image classifier and 24-hour ChatGPT suspensions for safety breaches
subtitle: The classifier — offered at no cost to vetted platforms through the OpenAI API — is paired with a 24-hour account hold inside ChatGPT when the system flags policy violations tied to minors.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI released an image classifier on November 16 aimed at detecting AI-generated child sexual abuse material, offered through its API at no cost to vetted companies and child-safety investigators. Alongside the classifier, ChatGPT itself now imposes a 24-hour account suspension when its own guardrails flag a user for violating OpenAI's rules protecting minors, with an appeals path through standard Trust and Safety review. The classifier is positioned as a dedicated CSAM detection endpoint — distinct from the free Moderation API, which OpenAI's developer docs explicitly state is not designed for CSAM and should not be relied on for it. Access is gated behind a vetting process to limit abuse of the tool itself.

The timing reflects a crisis the industry has been circling for 18 months. AI image generators have made synthetic CSAM materially easier to produce, and reporting pipelines run by NCMEC and the Internet Watch Foundation have logged a sharp rise in suspected AI-generated material alongside the known-content baseline. OpenAI, Thorn, Microsoft, Google, Meta and Hugging Face signed a joint set of Safety by Design principles last year, but the public tooling has lagged the problem. A free, dedicated classifier lowers the integration cost for smaller platforms that could not previously afford commercial CSAM detection.

There are open questions that a classifier alone does not resolve. Access gating means smaller volunteer-run communities may still struggle to onboard; false positives at any rate carry serious consequences in this domain; and detection of fully synthetic CSAM does not by itself close the legal grey area that has emerged in several jurisdictions over whether purely AI-generated depictions are prosecutable at all. OpenAI's 24-hour suspension mechanism also puts the first appeals burden on the user, which civil-liberties groups will watch — particularly as similar automated-moderation systems at other platforms have struggled with historical over-enforcement on art, education and medical contexts.

A note for learners: Trust and Safety is one of the most underinvested specialties in AI engineering, and one of the fastest-growing. If you want work that combines ML, policy and user-impact judgment, platforms shipping tools like this are hiring for roles that did not exist five years ago. The skills that transfer most directly are classification evaluation, policy-to-label translation, red-teaming, and the harder human work of building appeals processes that treat users as adults.
